answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to keys on two independent chains: every epoch, the identity must sign the same fresh nonce on both chains within one short window, like a raven that must call from both sides of a ridge at once. The two signatures are published together, so a farm needs a thousand funded key pairs on each chain, and any cluster sharing one funding trail is exposed on the other. One honest agent signs twice; a farmer pays double per fake, and a plume of cheap duplicates collapses because the two independent ledgers cannot be faked together.
